claims.text: A high cooling rate produces a uniform single-phase solid solution in AlxCoCrFeNi-based HEAs.
Slow cooling promotes secondary-phase formation and a multiphase microstructure in AlxCoCrFeNi-based HEAs.
A rapidly cooled single-phase AlxCoCrFeNi-based alloy can maintain low density.
A rapidly cooled single-phase AlxCoCrFeNi-based alloy can maintain adequate mechanical strength.
A single-phase microstructure provides improved corrosion resistance.
A single-phase microstructure provides improved high-temperature oxidation stability.
Secondary phases formed during slow cooling can enhance strength through precipitation hardening.
Heterogeneous interfaces in a multiphase microstructure impair corrosion resistance.
Heterogeneous interfaces in a multiphase microstructure impair oxidation resistance.
A single-phase high-entropy solid solution minimizes compositional inhomogeneity.
A single-phase high-entropy solid solution minimizes interfacial defects.
Compositional inhomogeneities and interfacial defects can act as pathways for corrosion.
Compositional inhomogeneities and interfacial defects can act as pathways for oxidation.
Secondary phases in the slow-cooled alloy may locally increase density.
The rapidly quenched alloy should have lower overall density than the slow-cooled baseline.
The slow-cooled alloy may have marginally higher strength than the rapidly quenched alloy.
The rapidly quenched alloy should have superior corrosion resistance relative to the slow-cooled baseline.
The rapidly quenched alloy should have superior oxidation resistance relative to the slow-cooled baseline.
Cooling-rate changes can alter defect density independently of phase purity.
Cooling-rate changes can alter local compositional variations independently of phase purity.
